documents.title: Climate transition risk reference data set documentation

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document describes the reference data set (RDS) of the Climate Transition Risk – Mortgages and Corporates model (model identifier MDL-19, model version 1.0, hereafter CTR) and the assessment of its data quality. The RDS serves the two CTR modules: the mortgage module for Dutch owner-occupied residential mortgages and the corporate module for the non-retail corporate lending portfolio booked in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. The intended use of the model is the quantification of climate transition risk in the ICAAP (normative and economic perspectives) and in the annual internal climate stress test under ERM-STD-300 §10; secondary uses are the C&E materiality assessment and the forward-looking metrics of the prudential transition plan. The document follows the RDS template of MRM-STD-021 Annex A; sections added to the template are numbered after the last template section of the relevant chapter, and template sections that do not apply are retained with the statement "Not applicable" and a justification. Physical risk data are outside the scope of this RDS; they are held in the Sustainability Risk physical risk data mart and are only combined with CTR results at aggregation level (MDD §2.4).

sections.heading: Data governance and ownership
sections.text: The data domains from which the RDS is sourced are mapped in the Group Data Catalogue: Retail Lending (mortgage loans and collateral), Wholesale Lending (corporate facilities and ratings), Counterparty Reference Data (legal entity identifiers and NACE codes), Sustainability Data (energy labels and emissions) and Market and Scenario Data. Each domain has exactly one Data Owner recorded in the catalogue; the Sustainability Data domain is owned by the ESG Data Lead of the Chief Data Office, who is also accountable for the vendor emissions data. The Model Owner agreed the data quality expectations for the 47 critical data elements of CTR with the five Data Owners in data quality agreement DQA-CTR-01 of 29 January 2027. Changes to the definition, source or transformation of a CTR data element are approved by the Data Owner through the catalogue change workflow and notified to the Model Owner at least 20 business days before they take effect. Roles for the ownership and quality of risk data are defined for business and IT: Data Owners and Data Stewards are accountable for source quality, the ESG data platform team in IT operates the ingestion pipelines, and Sustainability Risk Modelling is responsible for the RDS build. Climate-related data are governed within the Bank's general data governance framework (DATA-POL-001), IT infrastructure and risk data aggregation architecture rather than in a separate climate data silo; the ESG data platform introduced in 2024 systematically collects energy labels and counterparty emissions for all in-scope portfolios. For portfolios outside the CTR scope (SME retail and consumer lending), interim qualitative sector heatmaps remain in use, and their limitations are reported to the Management Board with the materiality assessment.

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: The RDS consists of four components with different observation periods. (1) Starting-point portfolio: the mortgage and corporate portfolios at the reference date 31 December 2026, comprising 612,400 mortgage loans (EUR 148.6 billion outstanding) secured on 598,900 residential properties, and 3,850 corporate obligors (EUR 41.3 billion drawn and EUR 9.8 billion undrawn committed). (2) Affordability panel: monthly snapshots from January 2015 to December 2024 taken from the frozen PD-MORT-NL reference data set RDS-MORT-NL v4.0, comprising 7,301,882 account-months for 702,000 unique facilities with 2,380 default events. (3) Hedonic transaction sample: 1,262,000 residential transactions registered by the Kadaster between January 2019 and December 2025, of which 918,400 carry a registered energy label valid at the transaction date. (4) Corporate migration panel: annual obligor observations from 2014 to 2025 taken from the corporate rating system, comprising 38,900 obligor-years for 6,120 unique obligors with 548 default events. Counts after exclusions are given in section 4.2 and the rebuild counts in chapter 8.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The affordability panel starts in January 2015 because registered energy labels are available at scale in the national register EP-Online only from 2015 onwards, and ends in December 2024 in line with the frozen RDS-MORT-NL v4.0. It covers the 2015–2019 recovery, the pandemic period and the 2022 energy price shock, during which household gas tariffs more than doubled; this episode is the only observed stress in household energy affordability and is essential to identify the energy-cost channel. The window does not contain a housing market downturn comparable to 2012–2013; the downturn behaviour of PD and LGD is therefore taken from the approved satellite models of MDL-10, and CTR only adds the label-differentiated component on top of it. The corporate migration panel covers 2014–2025 and includes the 2020 pandemic recession and the 2022–2023 energy crisis, which affected energy-intensive sectors disproportionately. The hedonic sample starts in 2019 to limit the mixing of label methods before and after the NTA 8800 method change of 1 January 2021; transactions in 2019–2020 with old-method labels are converted with the RVO conversion table (EJ-CTR-03).

sections.heading: Starting-point portfolio composition
sections.text: At 31 December 2026 the energy label distribution of the mortgage collateral, by exposure, is: A and better 29.8%, B 13.6%, C 23.1%, D 12.2%, E 8.4%, F 6.3% and G 6.6%. Registered labels cover 65.1% of mortgage exposure; the remaining 34.9% carries an estimated label (section 4.1.2). The corporate portfolio is mapped to 22 transition-risk sectors; the six transition-sensitive sector groups (fossil fuel extraction and supply, power generation, energy-intensive industry, transport, agriculture and construction materials) represent 42.4% of drawn exposure (EUR 17.5 billion), with the largest single-sector concentration in power generation (6.8%). All exposures are captured by legal entity, business line, product, country and sector, including off-balance-sheet commitments. The label distribution and the sector exposures are reconciled to the Pillar 3 ESG disclosure templates of 31 December 2026 (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2453, templates 1 and 2), with differences below 0.1% of exposure.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: CTR has no single default-based target; each estimated component has its own target variable and outcome horizon. The affordability component uses the 12-month default indicator of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 (default within the 12 months following the snapshot) as target. The hedonic component uses the logarithm of the transaction price as target, and the corporate migration component uses the one-year rating migration and the one-year default indicator of the corporate rating system. Scenario projections are produced annually over 2027–2029 for the ICAAP horizon and in five-year steps to 2050 for the long-term scenario analysis; these projections are model outputs and not part of the RDS.

sections.heading: Deviations from the Bank's definition of default
sections.text: CTR uses the default flags of the approved PD-MORT-NL and corporate rating reference data sets without modification, and no deviation from CR-STD-110 is introduced by CTR. For January–December 2015 the mortgage default flag is the historically approximated flag described in RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 section 6.2, which was reconstructed from arrears data before the implementation of the new definition of default. The energy-cost coefficient of the affordability model was re-estimated excluding 2015 as a sensitivity; the coefficient changed by 2.4% and the mortgage results by 0.9% (MDD §7.4). The approximation is recorded in the data deficiency log of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 and is not duplicated in the CTR log.

sections.heading: Default definition
sections.text: Mortgage default flags are inherited from RDS-MORT-NL v4.0: the days-past-due criterion (more than 90 days past due above the materiality threshold of EUR 100 and 1%) is assessed per facility, and unlikeliness-to-pay triggers are applied at obligor level. Corporate defaults are applied at obligor level with the non-retail materiality threshold of EUR 500 and 1% and the unlikeliness-to-pay triggers of the corporate default register. The only historical approximation affecting CTR is the approximated mortgage default flag for 2015 (section 3.2). All 548 default events of the corporate migration panel were reconciled to the default register maintained under CR-STD-110 without differences, and the mortgage default events were reconciled in the construction of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0. The RDS labels the prudential default flag (DEF_CRR) and the IFRS 9 credit-impaired indicator (STAGE3_IFRS9) distinctly, documents the difference between the two definitions in Annex A, and uses only DEF_CRR as target.

sections.heading: Unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: Not applicable as a CTR-specific specification: CTR does not define unlikeliness-to-pay triggers of its own, because it reuses the default flags of the approved reference data sets. For completeness, the inherited mortgage triggers are distressed restructuring, forced sale of the collateral, bankruptcy of the obligor and specific credit risk adjustments, sourced from the arrears management system. The inherited corporate triggers additionally include the sale of a credit obligation at a material credit-related economic loss and the breach of material covenants where a waiver has been declined, sourced from the corporate lending system and the default register. Any future change to these triggers in the underlying models is assessed for its effect on CTR through the dependency process described in MDD §2.2.

sections.heading: Data sources and lineage
sections.text: Source systems are the mortgage administration system (MAS), the collateral valuation database (CVD), the corporate lending system (CLS), the corporate rating system (CRS), the counterparty reference data hub (CRDH), the ESG data platform (ESGDP) and the scenario repository of Enterprise Stress Testing (SCN-REPO). For each type of data an authoritative source is designated: MAS for mortgage balances, CVD for indexed collateral values, EP-Online (received via ESGDP) for registered energy labels, CLS for corporate exposures, CRS for approved ratings and CRDH for NACE codes and legal entity identifiers. Extraction reference dates are 31 December 2026 for the starting-point portfolio (extraction run of 8 January 2027) and the frozen versions stated in section 2.1 for the historical panels. The lineage of each of the 64 RDS variables, including the 17 discarded variables used to construct retained variables, is documented in Annex A from source table and field through the landing zone, ESGDP and the model data lake to the RDS field, with a reference to the performing build script or ETL job and the extraction frequency and timing. Data are aggregated automatically by the build pipeline; the only manual inputs are the three expert mapping tables described in section 4.1.7. ESGDP is refreshed monthly and the full RDS quarterly; the RDS for the annual ICAAP run is available within 15 business days of the reference date, and the pipeline can be re-run for ad hoc stress tests at any month-end.

sections.heading: Energy label data
sections.text: Registered energy labels are obtained from the national register EP-Online operated by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) through the monthly bulk delivery; the lineage starts at receipt of the delivery file in ESGDP and records the provider (RVO), the data product (EP-Online bulk file) and the delivery date. Labels are matched to collateral on the BAG address identifier (verblijfsobject-ID) supplied by the Kadaster; 97.8% of properties have a valid BAG identifier, and the remainder are matched on postcode and house number. Where several registered labels exist, the most recent label valid at the reference date is used; labels registered under the NTA 8800 method (since 1 January 2021) and under the former method are distinguished by the variable EL_METHOD. Registered labels are the primary label input for collateral valuation in CTR, in line with CER-POL-001 §9.1, and the label and address of each property are refreshed in CVD at every revaluation.

sections.heading: Estimated energy labels
sections.text: For the 34.9% of mortgage exposure without a registered label, an estimated label is derived with the Bank's label estimation method EL-EST v2, an ordered logit on construction year, dwelling type, floor area, BAG building characteristics and neighbourhood-level label distributions. Estimated labels are flagged (EL_SOURCE = 'EST') and never overwrite registered labels. EL-EST v2 is owned by the Chief Data Office and was reviewed by Model Validation in 2025 (review memo MV-2025-117); on a hold-out of 48,000 properties with registered labels it assigns the exact label class in 58.6% and the class within one step in 91.2% of cases. Estimated labels are biased towards the middle classes: on the hold-out, 14.2% of G-labelled properties are estimated as E or better, which understates the share of F and G labels in the unlabelled population (deficiency DD-CTR-03). The share of estimated labels is reported per portfolio in every monitoring report and in the ICAAP results pack, and the resulting uncertainty is addressed in the MDD (chapter 6).

sections.heading: Property transaction and collateral data
sections.text: Transaction prices are taken from the Kadaster transaction register, delivered quarterly under the Bank's licence (delivery of 15 January 2026 for transactions up to December 2025), and are joined to EP-Online labels and BAG building characteristics. The Kadaster and EP-Online deliveries are stored with their delivery identifiers, so that each hedonic estimation can be traced to the exact data versions used. Collateral values in CVD are independent valuations at origination, indexed quarterly with the Kadaster/CBS house price index by region and dwelling type and revalued at least every three years, in line with CR-POL-001 §8.3. Collateral type, value, valuation date and method, lien rank and the link to the secured loan parts are recorded in CVD and subject to the DQ rules of section 6.1.1.

sections.heading: Corporate counterparty and sector data
sections.text: Corporate exposures (drawn amounts, undrawn committed amounts and collateral) are taken from CLS and approved ratings from CRS; legal entity identifiers, group structure and the NACE Rev. 2 code at four-digit level are taken from CRDH. The NACE code is mapped to 22 transition-risk sectors with the mapping table CTR-MAP-NACE v1.2, which extends the climate policy relevant sectors (CPRS) classification with the sector split of the NGFS Phase V output (for example iron and steel, cement, chemicals, road freight and livestock farming). Obligors whose primary NACE code does not reflect their main activity (holding companies, NACE 64.20) are re-mapped on the basis of the consolidated revenue split reported in the credit file; 212 obligors (EUR 3.1 billion) are re-mapped in this way. The re-mapping is an expert judgement in data treatment recorded as EJ-CTR-02 and is cross-referenced to data deficiency DD-CTR-04 in the data deficiency log. Obligors are additionally identified as directly or indirectly exposed to transition risk in the RDS (variable OBL_TR_EXPOSURE), using the thresholds of MDD §4.4.

sections.heading: Emissions data
sections.text: Scope 1 and 2 emissions per obligor are taken, in order of preference, from reported data (CSRD sustainability statements under ESRS E1 or annual reports; 34.2% of drawn exposure), from the external ESG data vendor under contract TPR-2025-0312 (vendor-estimated data; 28.9%), or from PCAF sector-average emission factors per unit of revenue (36.9%). Scope 3 emissions are included for oil and gas, automotive and chemicals, where they are material for transition risk. Financed emissions are attributed with the PCAF attribution factor (outstanding amount over enterprise value including cash for listed companies, or over total equity and debt for private companies), and each estimate carries the PCAF data quality score from 1 (verified reported emissions) to 5 (revenue-based sector average); the exposure-weighted score is 3.4. During vendor due diligence the Bank reviewed the vendor's methodology document (version 2026.1), its coverage and its estimation models for non-reporting companies, and documented the known limitations, in particular the use of sector-average intensities for 41% of the vendor's estimated values. Counterparty emissions and transition plans are collected at origination and refreshed at each annual credit review through the ESG questionnaire in CLS; at the reference date, 81% of obligors in transition-sensitive sectors had a questionnaire updated within the last 12 months. Reasonability checks compare reported emission intensities with sector ranges; in 2026, 37 questionnaires were challenged by the credit analysts and 22 were corrected.

sections.heading: Scenario data
sections.text: Scenario variables are sourced from SCN-REPO, which holds the NGFS Phase V scenario database (November 2024 release; integrated assessment model output for carbon prices and energy system variables, and NiGEM output for the Dutch, Belgian and German macroeconomic variables) and the NGFS short-term scenarios (May 2025 release). Macroeconomic paths of the ICAAP 2027 baseline and adverse scenarios are taken from the approved scenario generation model MDL-10 (release ICAAP-2027-v1.1 of 14 January 2027). Each scenario file is stored with its release identifier, and the lineage records the provider (NGFS scenario portal hosted by IIASA), the data product and release, and the download date (NGFS Phase V database downloaded on 20 November 2025). Scenario files are read-only once loaded into SCN-REPO; replacement by a new vintage requires a change request approved by Enterprise Stress Testing and the CTR Model Owner.

sections.heading: Manual inputs and end-user computing
sections.text: Three manual inputs are used, each held as a version-controlled CSV file in the build repository and documented as an expert judgement: the NACE-to-sector mapping CTR-MAP-NACE v1.2 (EJ-CTR-02), the label conversion table for pre-2021 labels (EJ-CTR-03) and the renovation cost table per label step (EJ-CTR-05). No other manual data manipulation takes place in the RDS build, and no end-user computing tool is used. Each change to a manual input file requires a merge request approved by a second developer, and the lineage in Annex A identifies each file explicitly as a manual input together with this control. Manual workarounds outside the build pipeline are not permitted; the build log records the file version of each manual input used.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Six exclusions are applied; each is listed with reason, records, exposure share and default events, and the conclusion of its impact analysis is given in section 5.3. E1: 3,410 defaulted mortgage loans (EUR 0.61 billion, 0.4% of exposure) are excluded from the PD uplift because their PD is already 100%; they remain in scope for the stressed LGD. E2: 61,300 transactions (4.9% of the hedonic sample) are excluded from the hedonic sample: related-party sales, auctions, and prices outside EUR 50,000–5,000,000 or outside the 0.5th–99.5th percentile of the price per square metre per municipality. E3: 71 defaulted corporate obligors (EUR 0.52 billion) are excluded from the rating migration and retained for LGD. E4: 38 public sector entities (EUR 0.90 billion) are excluded because they are covered by the sovereign stress module. E5: 1,940 obligor-years (5.0% of the corporate migration panel, 8 default events) without financial statements are excluded from the migration panel. E6: 1,020 mortgage loans on properties that could not be matched to any address (0.2% of exposure) are excluded from the hedonic join only and receive an imputed label (section 4.3). No exclusion exceeds 5% of records or exposure in any segment, except E2 for the province of Groningen (7.2% of transactions, caused by buy-outs under the earthquake damage scheme); this exclusion was approved by the Model Owner on 19 February 2027 and reported to Model Validation.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Missing values are classified per variable in Annex C as missing at random, missing for a structural reason or missing because of a data deficiency. Energy labels missing because no label was ever registered (structural) are replaced by the EL-EST v2 estimate; labels missing because of a failed address match (data deficiency, 0.3% of properties) are imputed with the neighbourhood modal label and recorded in deficiency DD-CTR-01. Obligor revenue missing for 2.1% of corporate obligors (structural, newly onboarded holding entities) is imputed from the most recent financial statement in the credit file. The share of imputed values is reported per variable in Annex C; re-estimating the hedonic and affordability models without imputed records changes the label coefficients by less than 3% (MDD §7.4). Outliers are identified with documented rules applied identically in development and in production runs: reported emission intensities outside the 1st–99th percentile of the sector distribution are verified against the source report and, if not confirmed, replaced by the vendor estimate. The outlier treatments change the ICAAP climate losses by less than 0.5%. The target variables (default indicators and transaction prices) are never imputed; records with a missing target value are excluded (none in the affordability panel, 0.4% of the hedonic sample).

sections.heading: Critical data elements and metadata
sections.text: All 47 model input variables and the data elements used to construct the target variables (default indicators, transaction prices and rating grades) are designated critical data elements (CDEs). Each CDE has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one DQ rule for each applicable data quality dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3 (Annex A and DQ rule book DQR-CTR v1.0). Metadata for each element (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The catalogue versions metadata, so that the definition applicable at any historical reference date can be retrieved; this is relevant in particular for the energy label method change of 2021. Consistent identifiers are used across the RDS: the Bank's counterparty identifier and the LEI for obligors, the facility key of the lending systems and the BAG identifier for properties, following the Group data taxonomy.

sections.heading: Data change control and dispensations
sections.text: The lineage in Annex A is updated before any changed source, transformation or data flow is used in development, monitoring or production; the change from EP-Online bulk file format version 3 to version 4 in November 2026 was reflected in lineage version 1.3 before the 31 December 2026 extraction. The lineage of the development data and of the production input data used by the stress testing platform was compared at the implementation dry run of April 2027: the only difference is that production reads the ESG data mart view ESG_DM.V_COLL_LABEL instead of the landing table, with identical content at the 31 December 2026 reference date and no effect on model outputs (EVD-19-ITR §5). Any deviation from DATA-POL-001 affecting CTR data would require a dispensation approved by the Chief Data Officer and the Head of Model Risk Management with an expiry date of at most twelve months; no such dispensation is in place.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: Representativeness is assessed for each estimated component against the portfolio at 31 December 2026; detailed tables are in Annex B. For the affordability panel, the PSI between the panel and the current portfolio is 0.06 on the label distribution, 0.08 on indexed LTV bucket and 0.11 on loan-to-income bucket; the amber value on loan-to-income reflects the higher incomes of recent vintages and is not considered to bias the energy-cost elasticity. Default-rate levels are compared per label group: the panel default rate is 0.41% for labels A–C, 0.52% for D–E and 0.63% for F–G, against 0.33%, 0.44% and 0.57% observed in the current portfolio in 2025–2026; the differences are not significant at 5% for any group. The hedonic sample reproduces the label distribution of the mortgage collateral within 2.5 percentage points per class but under-represents the provinces of Zeeland and Limburg (PSI 0.07 on province). For the corporate panel, the sector mix of 2014–2025 differs from the current portfolio in the share of power generation (4.1% versus 6.8% of exposure), which is addressed by sector-specific calibration in the MDD. Validity and uniqueness were assessed together with representativeness: no duplicate loan, property or obligor keys exist in the RDS.

sections.heading: Representativeness for other uses
sections.text: CTR outputs are also used as input to the annual C&E materiality assessment and for the forward-looking metrics of the prudential transition plan (portfolio alignment and label distribution). For these uses the starting-point portfolio is identical to that of the ICAAP run, so no additional population is involved. CTR is not used for Belgian or German mortgages or for commercial real estate, which are outside the RDS population; these portfolios are covered by the qualitative assessment of Sustainability Risk.

sections.heading: Impact of exclusions
sections.text: Excluding defaulted exposures (E1 and E3) from the PD uplift has no effect on the label distribution of the non-defaulted portfolio (maximum difference 0.1 percentage point per class). Exclusion E2 shifts the hedonic label coefficients by at most 0.4 percentage points; re-estimation including the Groningen buy-outs increases the G-label price differential from −7.8% to −8.3%, which is within the confidence interval of the estimate. Exclusion E5 raises the default rate of the corporate migration panel from 1.41% to 1.46%; migration matrices estimated with and without the excluded obligor-years differ by less than one notch in 98% of cells. Exclusions E4 and E6 have no effect on risk-driver distributions of more than 0.1 percentage point. The analysis concludes that no exclusion materially changes the label or sector distribution or the default rates of the RDS.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: The DQ assessment of the RDS was performed from 1 to 23 February 2027 on the candidate RDS before development and is reported in EVD-19-DQR; it covers completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness for every CDE and, where relevant, validity, uniqueness and appropriateness. All 47 CDEs pass their thresholds; energy label completeness (65.1% registered) and reported emissions completeness (34.2%) are assessed against the model-specific thresholds of section 6.1.1. The assessment concludes that the RDS is fit for the intended use in the ICAAP and in climate stress testing, subject to the deficiencies in section 6.2, and was signed off by the lead developer and the Model Owner on 26 February 2027 before the RDS was frozen. Model estimation started on 1 March 2027, after the RDS sign-off by the Model Owner. Data quality of the CTR data is managed under MRM-STD-022, and the same assessment will be repeated on every new RDS version and on the data used for each periodic validation.

sections.heading: DQ rules and thresholds
sections.text: 126 DQ rules are defined for the 47 CDEs: 47 completeness, 29 accuracy, 31 consistency and 19 timeliness rules, supplemented by validity and uniqueness checks on identifiers. Where a mandatory dimension is not applicable to a CDE (for example timeliness for static entries of the NACE mapping table), the reason is recorded in the rule book DQR-CTR v1.0, which forms part of this documentation. Thresholds are the defaults of MRM-STD-022 §4.3, with two justified deviations approved by the Model Owner on 19 February 2027: completeness of registered energy labels is measured against amber 60% and red 55% of exposure because the gap is structural and filled with flagged estimates, and completeness of reported emissions against amber 30% and red 25% of exposure because the three-tier hierarchy guarantees a value for every obligor. Thresholds for the target-related CDEs (default indicator, default date and transaction price) are the default thresholds without relaxation. Recurring checks for all rules are implemented in the Group DQ monitoring tool (rule set DQM-CTR-01) and are also executed on the production input data of every stress test run before the CTR module starts.

sections.heading: Reconciliation to source systems and finance
sections.text: Starting-point exposures are reconciled to the general ledger and to the FINREP and COREP reports of 31 December 2026: mortgage outstanding EUR 148.6 billion (difference to the ledger 0.02%) and corporate drawn EUR 41.3 billion (difference 0.08%, explained by accrued interest). Undrawn committed amounts of EUR 9.8 billion are reconciled to the off-balance-sheet items reported in COREP. Record counts per reference date are reconciled to MAS and CLS without differences, and energy labels are reconciled to the RVO delivery file (100% of registered labels traced). CDEs are reconciled to the source systems at least annually and at each ICAAP run; unexplained differences are logged as data quality issues in the Bank data issue register. Controls over CTR data are therefore equivalent to those applied to accounting data, and the aggregation is performed by the automated pipeline with reconciliation checkpoints after each stage.

sections.heading: Completeness, consistency and timeliness
sections.text: Record-level completeness was confirmed: all in-scope loans, properties, obligors and default events are included, and attribute-level completeness is reported per CDE in EVD-19-DQR §3. Consistency is assessed between the RDS and the production input data of the stress testing platform (identical at the reference date), over the observation period (label method change of 2021 and the default definition change in the mortgage panel) and logically between related fields, for example a label registration date not later than the reference date (99.7% of records pass). Timeliness is measured as the lag between the reference date and data availability (EP-Online: 6 business days; vendor emissions: reporting year t−1 available in the third quarter of year t) and as the currency of refreshed items (median age of financial statements 9 months; collateral indexation quarterly).

sections.heading: Data deficiencies
sections.text: Five data deficiencies have been identified so far and are listed in the draft data deficiency log. DD-CTR-01 concerns failed address matches for 0.3% of properties; DD-CTR-02 the absence of a registered label for 34.9% of mortgage exposure; DD-CTR-03 the bias of estimated labels towards the middle classes; DD-CTR-04 incorrect NACE codes of holding companies; and DD-CTR-05 the reporting lag of vendor emissions. Treatments are being defined with the Data Owners; impacts, remediation owners and target dates will be added after the data quality assessment has been completed.

sections.heading: Personal data and fair treatment
sections.text: The mortgage part of the RDS contains personal data of borrowers (loan identifiers, income and property address), processed under Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR for the Bank's legal obligations under the CRR and CRD to assess its capital adequacy. The processing is covered by the DPIA for credit risk modelling DPIA-2026-118, extended to CTR on 14 December 2026 (DPIA-2026-118-A2). The RDS contains no protected attributes; addresses are used only to match energy labels and are pseudonymised after matching. CTR does not produce outputs on individual customers: the mortgage module is applied at loan level for aggregation only, and its results are not used in credit decisions, pricing or customer communication.

sections.heading: Archiving and retention
sections.text: Each RDS version used for development or recalibration (currently RDS-CTR-2026Q4 v1.0) is archived together with the build code tag, the lineage version and a snapshot of the catalogue metadata, so that the development data can be reproduced. Archived data are write-protected; a correction is made only by creating a new RDS version (for example v1.1) while the original version is retained.

sections.heading: Annex A – Data dictionary and lineage
sections.text: Annex A lists all 64 RDS variables: 47 retained model inputs and target constituents, and 17 discarded variables used to construct retained variables. sections.heading: Annex B – Representativeness analyses

sections.heading: Annex C – Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Annex C lists, for each of the 47 CDEs, the missing-value classification (at random, structural or data deficiency), the share missing, the treatment applied and its justification, and the share of imputed values. sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document describes the reference data set (RDS) of the Climate Transition Risk – Mortgages and Corporates model (model identifier MDL-19, model version 1.0, hereafter CTR) and the assessment of its data quality. The RDS serves the two CTR modules: the mortgage module for Dutch owner-occupied residential mortgages and the corporate module for the non-retail corporate lending portfolio booked in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. The intended use of the model is the quantification of climate transition risk in the ICAAP (normative and economic perspectives) and in the annual internal climate stress test under ERM-STD-300 §10; secondary uses are the C&E materiality assessment and the forward-looking metrics of the prudential transition plan. The document follows the RDS template of MRM-STD-021 Annex A; sections added to the template are numbered after the last template section of the relevant chapter, and template sections that do not apply are retained with the statement "Not applicable" and a justification. Physical risk data are outside the scope of this RDS; they are held in the Sustainability Risk physical risk data mart and are only combined with CTR results at aggregation level (MDD §2.4).

sections.heading: Data governance and ownership
sections.text: The data domains from which the RDS is sourced are mapped in the Group Data Catalogue: Retail Lending (mortgage loans and collateral), Wholesale Lending (corporate facilities and ratings), Counterparty Reference Data (legal entity identifiers and NACE codes), Sustainability Data (energy labels and emissions) and Market and Scenario Data. Each domain has exactly one Data Owner recorded in the catalogue; the Sustainability Data domain is owned by the ESG Data Lead of the Chief Data Office, who is also accountable for the vendor emissions data. The Model Owner agreed the data quality expectations for the 47 critical data elements of CTR with the five Data Owners in data quality agreement DQA-CTR-01 of 29 January 2027. Changes to the definition, source or transformation of a CTR data element are approved by the Data Owner through the catalogue change workflow and notified to the Model Owner at least 20 business days before they take effect. Roles for the ownership and quality of risk data are defined for business and IT: Data Owners and Data Stewards are accountable for source quality, the ESG data platform team in IT operates the ingestion pipelines, and Sustainability Risk Modelling is responsible for the RDS build. Climate-related data are governed within the Bank's general data governance framework (DATA-POL-001), IT infrastructure and risk data aggregation architecture rather than in a separate climate data silo; the ESG data platform introduced in 2024 systematically collects energy labels and counterparty emissions for all in-scope portfolios. For portfolios outside the CTR scope (SME retail and consumer lending), interim qualitative sector heatmaps remain in use, and their limitations are reported to the Management Board with the materiality assessment.

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: The RDS consists of four components with different observation periods. (1) Starting-point portfolio: the mortgage and corporate portfolios at the reference date 31 December 2026, comprising 612,400 mortgage loans (EUR 148.6 billion outstanding) secured on 598,900 residential properties, and 3,850 corporate obligors (EUR 41.3 billion drawn and EUR 9.8 billion undrawn committed). (2) Affordability panel: monthly snapshots from January 2015 to December 2024 taken from the frozen PD-MORT-NL reference data set RDS-MORT-NL v4.0, comprising 7,301,882 account-months for 702,000 unique facilities with 2,380 default events. (3) Hedonic transaction sample: 1,262,000 residential transactions registered by the Kadaster between January 2019 and December 2025, of which 918,400 carry a registered energy label valid at the transaction date. (4) Corporate migration panel: annual obligor observations from 2014 to 2025 taken from the corporate rating system, comprising 38,900 obligor-years for 6,120 unique obligors with 548 default events. Counts after exclusions are given in section 4.2 and the rebuild counts in chapter 8.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The affordability panel starts in January 2015 because registered energy labels are available at scale in the national register EP-Online only from 2015 onwards, and ends in December 2024 in line with the frozen RDS-MORT-NL v4.0. It covers the 2015–2019 recovery, the pandemic period and the 2022 energy price shock, during which household gas tariffs more than doubled; this episode is the only observed stress in household energy affordability and is essential to identify the energy-cost channel. The window does not contain a housing market downturn comparable to 2012–2013; the downturn behaviour of PD and LGD is therefore taken from the approved satellite models of MDL-10, and CTR only adds the label-differentiated component on top of it. The corporate migration panel covers 2014–2025 and includes the 2020 pandemic recession and the 2022–2023 energy crisis, which affected energy-intensive sectors disproportionately. The hedonic sample starts in 2019 to limit the mixing of label methods before and after the NTA 8800 method change of 1 January 2021; transactions in 2019–2020 with old-method labels are converted with the RVO conversion table (EJ-CTR-03).

sections.heading: Starting-point portfolio composition
sections.text: At 31 December 2026 the energy label distribution of the mortgage collateral, by exposure, is: A and better 29.8%, B 13.6%, C 23.1%, D 12.2%, E 8.4%, F 6.3% and G 6.6%. Registered labels cover 65.1% of mortgage exposure; the remaining 34.9% carries an estimated label (section 4.1.2). The corporate portfolio is mapped to 22 transition-risk sectors; the six transition-sensitive sector groups (fossil fuel extraction and supply, power generation, energy-intensive industry, transport, agriculture and construction materials) represent 42.4% of drawn exposure (EUR 17.5 billion), with the largest single-sector concentration in power generation (6.8%). All exposures are captured by legal entity, business line, product, country and sector, including off-balance-sheet commitments. The label distribution and the sector exposures are reconciled to the Pillar 3 ESG disclosure templates of 31 December 2026 (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2453, templates 1 and 2), with differences below 0.1% of exposure.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: CTR has no single default-based target; each estimated component has its own target variable and outcome horizon. The affordability component uses the 12-month default indicator of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 (default within the 12 months following the snapshot) as target. The hedonic component uses the logarithm of the transaction price as target, and the corporate migration component uses the one-year rating migration and the one-year default indicator of the corporate rating system. Scenario projections are produced annually over 2027–2029 for the ICAAP horizon and in five-year steps to 2050 for the long-term scenario analysis; these projections are model outputs and not part of the RDS.

sections.heading: Deviations from the Bank's definition of default
sections.text: CTR uses the default flags of the approved PD-MORT-NL and corporate rating reference data sets without modification, and no deviation from CR-STD-110 is introduced by CTR. For January–December 2015 the mortgage default flag is the historically approximated flag described in RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 section 6.2, which was reconstructed from arrears data before the implementation of the new definition of default. The energy-cost coefficient of the affordability model was re-estimated excluding 2015 as a sensitivity; the coefficient changed by 2.4% and the mortgage results by 0.9% (MDD §7.4). The approximation is recorded in the data deficiency log of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 and is not duplicated in the CTR log.

sections.heading: Default definition
sections.text: Mortgage default flags are inherited from RDS-MORT-NL v4.0: the days-past-due criterion (more than 90 days past due above the materiality threshold of EUR 100 and 1%) is assessed per facility, and unlikeliness-to-pay triggers are applied at obligor level. Corporate defaults are applied at obligor level with the non-retail materiality threshold of EUR 500 and 1% and the unlikeliness-to-pay triggers of the corporate default register. The only historical approximation affecting CTR is the approximated mortgage default flag for 2015 (section 3.2). All 548 default events of the corporate migration panel were reconciled to the default register maintained under CR-STD-110 without differences, and the mortgage default events were reconciled in the construction of RDS-MORT-NL v4.0. The RDS labels the prudential default flag (DEF_CRR) and the IFRS 9 credit-impaired indicator (STAGE3_IFRS9) distinctly, documents the difference between the two definitions in Annex A, and uses only DEF_CRR as target.

sections.heading: Unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: Not applicable as a CTR-specific specification: CTR does not define unlikeliness-to-pay triggers of its own, because it reuses the default flags of the approved reference data sets. For completeness, the inherited mortgage triggers are distressed restructuring, forced sale of the collateral, bankruptcy of the obligor and specific credit risk adjustments, sourced from the arrears management system. The inherited corporate triggers additionally include the sale of a credit obligation at a material credit-related economic loss and the breach of material covenants where a waiver has been declined, sourced from the corporate lending system and the default register. Any future change to these triggers in the underlying models is assessed for its effect on CTR through the dependency process described in MDD §2.2.

sections.heading: Data sources and lineage

For each type of data an authoritative source is designated: MAS for mortgage balances, CVD for indexed collateral values, EP-Online (received via ESGDP) for registered energy labels, CLS for corporate exposures, CRS for approved ratings and CRDH for NACE codes and legal entity identifiers. Extraction reference dates are 31 December 2026 for the starting-point portfolio (extraction run of 8 January 2027) and the frozen versions stated in section 2.1 for the historical panels. The lineage of each of the 64 RDS variables, including the 17 discarded variables used to construct retained variables, is documented in Annex A from source table and field through the landing zone, ESGDP and the model data lake to the RDS field, with a reference to the performing build script or ETL job and the extraction frequency and timing. Data are aggregated automatically by the build pipeline; the only manual inputs are the three expert mapping tables described in section 4.1.7. ESGDP is refreshed monthly and the full RDS quarterly; the RDS for the annual ICAAP run is available within 15 business days of the reference date, and the pipeline can be re-run for ad hoc stress tests at any month-end.

sections.heading: Energy label data
sections.text: Registered energy labels are obtained from the national register EP-Online operated by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) through the monthly bulk delivery; the lineage starts at receipt of the delivery file in ESGDP and records the provider (RVO), the data product (EP-Online bulk file) and the delivery date. Labels are matched to collateral on the BAG address identifier (verblijfsobject-ID) supplied by the Kadaster; 97.8% of properties have a valid BAG identifier, and the remainder are matched on postcode and house number. Where several registered labels exist, the most recent label valid at the reference date is used; labels registered under the NTA 8800 method (since 1 January 2021) and under the former method are distinguished by the variable EL_METHOD. Registered labels are the primary label input for collateral valuation in CTR, in line with CER-POL-001 §9.1, and the label and address of each property are refreshed in CVD at every revaluation.

sections.heading: Estimated energy labels
sections.text: For the 34.9% of mortgage exposure without a registered label, an estimated label is derived with the Bank's label estimation method EL-EST v2, an ordered logit on construction year, dwelling type, floor area, BAG building characteristics and neighbourhood-level label distributions. Estimated labels are flagged (EL_SOURCE = 'EST') and never overwrite registered labels. EL-EST v2 is owned by the Chief Data Office and was reviewed by Model Validation in 2025 (review memo MV-2025-117); on a hold-out of 48,000 properties with registered labels it assigns the exact label class in 58.6% and the class within one step in 91.2% of cases. Estimated labels are biased towards the middle classes: on the hold-out, 14.2% of G-labelled properties are estimated as E or better, which understates the share of F and G labels in the unlabelled population (deficiency DD-CTR-03). The share of estimated labels is reported per portfolio in every monitoring report and in the ICAAP results pack, and the resulting uncertainty is addressed in the MDD (chapter 6).

sections.heading: Property transaction and collateral data
sections.text: Transaction prices are taken from the Kadaster transaction register, delivered quarterly under the Bank's licence (delivery of 15 January 2026 for transactions up to December 2025), and are joined to EP-Online labels and BAG building characteristics. The Kadaster and EP-Online deliveries are stored with their delivery identifiers, so that each hedonic estimation can be traced to the exact data versions used. Collateral values in CVD are independent valuations at origination, indexed quarterly with the Kadaster/CBS house price index by region and dwelling type and revalued at least every three years, in line with CR-POL-001 §8.3. Collateral type, value, valuation date and method, lien rank and the link to the secured loan parts are recorded in CVD and subject to the DQ rules of section 6.1.1.

sections.heading: Corporate counterparty and sector data
sections.text: Corporate exposures (drawn amounts, undrawn committed amounts and collateral) are taken from CLS and approved ratings from CRS; legal entity identifiers, group structure and the NACE Rev. 2 code at four-digit level are taken from CRDH. The NACE code is mapped to 22 transition-risk sectors with the mapping table CTR-MAP-NACE v1.2, which extends the climate policy relevant sectors (CPRS) classification with the sector split of the NGFS Phase V output (for example iron and steel, cement, chemicals, road freight and livestock farming). Obligors whose primary NACE code does not reflect their main activity (holding companies, NACE 64.20) are re-mapped on the basis of the consolidated revenue split reported in the credit file; 212 obligors (EUR 3.1 billion) are re-mapped in this way. The re-mapping is an expert judgement in data treatment recorded as EJ-CTR-02 and is cross-referenced to data deficiency DD-CTR-04 in the data deficiency log. Obligors are additionally identified as directly or indirectly exposed to transition risk in the RDS (variable OBL_TR_EXPOSURE), using the thresholds of MDD §4.4.

sections.heading: Emissions data
sections.text: Scope 1 and 2 emissions per obligor are taken, in order of preference, from reported data (CSRD sustainability statements under ESRS E1 or annual reports; 34.2% of drawn exposure), from the external ESG data vendor under contract TPR-2025-0312 (vendor-estimated data; 28.9%), or from PCAF sector-average emission factors per unit of revenue (36.9%). Scope 3 emissions are included for oil and gas, automotive and chemicals, where they are material for transition risk. Financed emissions are attributed with the PCAF attribution factor (outstanding amount over enterprise value including cash for listed companies, or over total equity and debt for private companies), and each estimate carries the PCAF data quality score from 1 (verified reported emissions) to 5 (revenue-based sector average); the exposure-weighted score is 3.4. During vendor due diligence the Bank reviewed the vendor's methodology document (version 2026.1), its coverage and its estimation models for non-reporting companies, and documented the known limitations, in particular the use of sector-average intensities for 41% of the vendor's estimated values. Counterparty emissions and transition plans are collected at origination and refreshed at each annual credit review through the ESG questionnaire in CLS; at the reference date, 81% of obligors in transition-sensitive sectors had a questionnaire updated within the last 12 months. Reasonability checks compare reported emission intensities with sector ranges; in 2026, 37 questionnaires were challenged by the credit analysts and 22 were corrected.

sections.heading: Scenario data
sections.text: Scenario variables are sourced from SCN-REPO, which holds the NGFS Phase V scenario database (November 2024 release; integrated assessment model output for carbon prices and energy system variables, and NiGEM output for the Dutch, Belgian and German macroeconomic variables) and the NGFS short-term scenarios (May 2025 release). Macroeconomic paths of the ICAAP 2027 baseline and adverse scenarios are taken from the approved scenario generation model MDL-10 (release ICAAP-2027-v1.1 of 14 January 2027). Each scenario file is stored with its release identifier, and the lineage records the provider (NGFS scenario portal hosted by IIASA), the data product and release, and the download date (NGFS Phase V database downloaded on 20 November 2025). Scenario files are read-only once loaded into SCN-REPO; replacement by a new vintage requires a change request approved by Enterprise Stress Testing and the CTR Model Owner.

sections.heading: Manual inputs and end-user computing
sections.text: Three manual inputs are used, each held as a version-controlled CSV file in the build repository and documented as an expert judgement: the NACE-to-sector mapping CTR-MAP-NACE v1.2 (EJ-CTR-02), the label conversion table for pre-2021 labels (EJ-CTR-03) and the renovation cost table per label step (EJ-CTR-05). No other manual data manipulation takes place in the RDS build, and no end-user computing tool is used. Each change to a manual input file requires a merge request approved by a second developer, and the lineage in Annex A identifies each file explicitly as a manual input together with this control. Manual workarounds outside the build pipeline are not permitted; the build log records the file version of each manual input used.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Six exclusions are applied; each is listed with reason, records, exposure share and default events, and the conclusion of its impact analysis is given in section 5.3. E1: 3,410 defaulted mortgage loans (EUR 0.61 billion, 0.4% of exposure) are excluded from the PD uplift because their PD is already 100%; they remain in scope for the stressed LGD. E2: 61,300 transactions (4.9% of the hedonic sample) are excluded from the hedonic sample: related-party sales, auctions, and prices outside EUR 50,000–5,000,000 or outside the 0.5th–99.5th percentile of the price per square metre per municipality. E3: 71 defaulted corporate obligors (EUR 0.52 billion) are excluded from the rating migration and retained for LGD. E4: 38 public sector entities (EUR 0.90 billion) are excluded because they are covered by the sovereign stress module. E5: 1,940 obligor-years (5.0% of the corporate migration panel, 8 default events) without financial statements are excluded from the migration panel. E6: 1,020 mortgage loans on properties that could not be matched to any address (0.2% of exposure) are excluded from the hedonic join only and receive an imputed label (section 4.3). No exclusion exceeds 5% of records or exposure in any segment, except E2 for the province of Groningen (7.2% of transactions, caused by buy-outs under the earthquake damage scheme); this exclusion was approved by the Model Owner on 19 February 2027 and reported to Model Validation.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Missing values are classified per variable in Annex C as missing at random, missing for a structural reason or missing because of a data deficiency. Energy labels missing because no label was ever registered (structural) are replaced by the EL-EST v2 estimate; labels missing because of a failed address match (data deficiency, 0.3% of properties) are imputed with the neighbourhood modal label and recorded in deficiency DD-CTR-01. Obligor revenue missing for 2.1% of corporate obligors (structural, newly onboarded holding entities) is imputed from the most recent financial statement in the credit file. The share of imputed values is reported per variable in Annex C; re-estimating the hedonic and affordability models without imputed records changes the label coefficients by less than 3% (MDD §7.4). Outliers are identified with documented rules applied identically in development and in production runs: reported emission intensities outside the 1st–99th percentile of the sector distribution are verified against the source report and, if not confirmed, replaced by the vendor estimate. The outlier treatments change the ICAAP climate losses by less than 0.5%. The target variables (default indicators and transaction prices) are never imputed; records with a missing target value are excluded (none in the affordability panel, 0.4% of the hedonic sample).

sections.heading: Critical data elements and metadata
sections.text: All 47 model input variables and the data elements used to construct the target variables (default indicators, transaction prices and rating grades) are designated critical data elements (CDEs). Each CDE has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one DQ rule for each applicable data quality dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3 (Annex A and DQ rule book DQR-CTR v1.0). Metadata for each element (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The catalogue versions metadata, so that the definition applicable at any historical reference date can be retrieved; this is relevant in particular for the energy label method change of 2021. Consistent identifiers are used across the RDS: the Bank's counterparty identifier and the LEI for obligors, the facility key of the lending systems and the BAG identifier for properties, following the Group data taxonomy.

sections.heading: Data change control and dispensations
sections.text: The lineage in Annex A is updated before any changed source, transformation or data flow is used in development, monitoring or production; the change from EP-Online bulk file format version 3 to version 4 in November 2026 was reflected in lineage version 1.3 before the 31 December 2026 extraction. The lineage of the development data and of the production input data used by the stress testing platform was compared at the implementation dry run of April 2027: the only difference is that production reads the ESG data mart view ESG_DM.V_COLL_LABEL instead of the landing table, with identical content at the 31 December 2026 reference date and no effect on model outputs (EVD-19-ITR §5). Any deviation from DATA-POL-001 affecting CTR data would require a dispensation approved by the Chief Data Officer and the Head of Model Risk Management with an expiry date of at most twelve months; no such dispensation is in place.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: Representativeness is assessed for each estimated component against the portfolio at 31 December 2026; detailed tables are in Annex B. For the affordability panel, the PSI between the panel and the current portfolio is 0.06 on the label distribution, 0.08 on indexed LTV bucket and 0.11 on loan-to-income bucket; the amber value on loan-to-income reflects the higher incomes of recent vintages and is not considered to bias the energy-cost elasticity. Default-rate levels are compared per label group: the panel default rate is 0.41% for labels A–C, 0.52% for D–E and 0.63% for F–G, against 0.33%, 0.44% and 0.57% observed in the current portfolio in 2025–2026; the differences are not significant at 5% for any group. The hedonic sample reproduces the label distribution of the mortgage collateral within 2.5 percentage points per class but under-represents the provinces of Zeeland and Limburg (PSI 0.07 on province). For the corporate panel, the sector mix of 2014–2025 differs from the current portfolio in the share of power generation (4.1% versus 6.8% of exposure), which is addressed by sector-specific calibration in the MDD. Validity and uniqueness were assessed together with representativeness: no duplicate loan, property or obligor keys exist in the RDS.

sections.heading: Representativeness for other uses
sections.text: CTR outputs are also used as input to the annual C&E materiality assessment and for the forward-looking metrics of the prudential transition plan (portfolio alignment and label distribution). For these uses the starting-point portfolio is identical to that of the ICAAP run, so no additional population is involved. CTR is not used for Belgian or German mortgages or for commercial real estate, which are outside the RDS population; these portfolios are covered by the qualitative assessment of Sustainability Risk.

sections.heading: Impact of exclusions
sections.text: Excluding defaulted exposures (E1 and E3) from the PD uplift has no effect on the label distribution of the non-defaulted portfolio (maximum difference 0.1 percentage point per class). Exclusion E2 shifts the hedonic label coefficients by at most 0.4 percentage points; re-estimation including the Groningen buy-outs increases the G-label price differential from −7.8% to −8.3%, which is within the confidence interval of the estimate. Exclusion E5 raises the default rate of the corporate migration panel from 1.41% to 1.46%; migration matrices estimated with and without the excluded obligor-years differ by less than one notch in 98% of cells. Exclusions E4 and E6 have no effect on risk-driver distributions of more than 0.1 percentage point. The analysis concludes that no exclusion materially changes the label or sector distribution or the default rates of the RDS.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: The DQ assessment of the RDS was performed from 1 to 23 February 2027 on the candidate RDS before development and is reported in EVD-19-DQR; it covers completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness for every CDE and, where relevant, validity, uniqueness and appropriateness. All 47 CDEs pass their thresholds; energy label completeness (65.1% registered) and reported emissions completeness (34.2%) are assessed against the model-specific thresholds of section 6.1.1. The assessment concludes that the RDS is fit for the intended use in the ICAAP and in climate stress testing, subject to the deficiencies in section 6.2, and was signed off by the lead developer and the Model Owner on 26 February 2027 before the RDS was frozen. Model estimation started on 1 March 2027, after the RDS sign-off by the Model Owner. Data quality of the CTR data is managed under MRM-STD-022, and the same assessment will be repeated on every new RDS version and on the data used for each periodic validation.

sections.heading: DQ rules and thresholds
sections.text: 126 DQ rules are defined for the 47 CDEs: 47 completeness, 29 accuracy, 31 consistency and 19 timeliness rules, supplemented by validity and uniqueness checks on identifiers. Where a mandatory dimension is not applicable to a CDE (for example timeliness for static entries of the NACE mapping table), the reason is recorded in the rule book DQR-CTR v1.0, which forms part of this documentation. Thresholds are the defaults of MRM-STD-022 §4.3, with two justified deviations approved by the Model Owner on 19 February 2027: completeness of registered energy labels is measured against amber 60% and red 55% of exposure because the gap is structural and filled with flagged estimates, and completeness of reported emissions against amber 30% and red 25% of exposure because the three-tier hierarchy guarantees a value for every obligor. Thresholds for the target-related CDEs (default indicator, default date and transaction price) are the default thresholds without relaxation. Recurring checks for all rules are implemented in the Group DQ monitoring tool (rule set DQM-CTR-01) and are also executed on the production input data of every stress test run before the CTR module starts.

sections.heading: Reconciliation to source systems and finance
sections.text: Starting-point exposures are reconciled to the general ledger and to the FINREP and COREP reports of 31 December 2026: mortgage outstanding EUR 148.6 billion (difference to the ledger 0.02%) and corporate drawn EUR 41.3 billion (difference 0.08%, explained by accrued interest). Undrawn committed amounts of EUR 9.8 billion are reconciled to the off-balance-sheet items reported in COREP. Record counts per reference date are reconciled to MAS and CLS without differences, and energy labels are reconciled to the RVO delivery file (100% of registered labels traced). CDEs are reconciled to the source systems at least annually and at each ICAAP run; unexplained differences are logged as data quality issues in the Bank data issue register. Controls over CTR data are therefore equivalent to those applied to accounting data, and the aggregation is performed by the automated pipeline with reconciliation checkpoints after each stage.

sections.heading: Sample-based verification
sections.text: Because CTR results are used in the ICAAP, a sample-based verification against source documentation was performed although it is mandatory only for Tier 1 models. 300 properties were checked against the EP-Online register and the valuation report in the credit file, and 120 corporate obligors against the emissions published in their sustainability statements or annual reports. Label agreement was 99.3%, the two mismatches being caused by label re-registrations after the extraction date. For emissions, 7 of 120 obligors (5.8%) showed differences above 10%, all caused by the vendor using the prior reporting year; this is recorded as deficiency DD-CTR-05. Accuracy is thus measured by reconciliation to source systems and accounting data (section 6.1.2), by comparison with an independent source (EP-Online versus the valuation report) and by sample-based checks.

sections.heading: Completeness, consistency and timeliness
sections.text: Record-level completeness was confirmed: all in-scope loans, properties, obligors and default events are included, and attribute-level completeness is reported per CDE in EVD-19-DQR §3. Consistency is assessed between the RDS and the production input data of the stress testing platform (identical at the reference date), over the observation period (label method change of 2021 and the default definition change in the mortgage panel) and logically between related fields, for example a label registration date not later than the reference date (99.7% of records pass). Timeliness is measured as the lag between the reference date and data availability (EP-Online: 6 business days; vendor emissions: reporting year t−1 available in the third quarter of year t) and as the currency of refreshed items (median age of financial statements 9 months; collateral indexation quarterly).

sections.heading: Data deficiencies
sections.text: Five data deficiencies are recorded in the CTR data deficiency log, each with affected variables and segments, DQ dimension, cause, impact and treatment, and each is cross-referenced to the MDD limitations log. DD-CTR-01 (completeness, energy label): failed address matches for 0.3% of properties, imputed with the neighbourhood modal label; impact below 0.1% of mortgage losses; limitation L-03. DD-CTR-02 (appropriateness, energy label): no registered label for 34.9% of mortgage exposure; estimated labels used and treated by a methodological adjustment of +5% on mortgage module results (EJ-CTR-06); limitation L-03. DD-CTR-03 (accuracy, estimated label): EL-EST v2 understates the share of F and G labels in the unlabelled population; treated jointly with DD-CTR-02; limitation L-03. DD-CTR-04 (accuracy, NACE code): the primary NACE code of holding companies does not reflect their activity; corrected by re-mapping (EJ-CTR-02); impact +1.8% on corporate losses; limitation L-06. DD-CTR-05 (timeliness, emissions): vendor emissions lag the latest reporting year for 5.8% of verified obligors; treated by overriding with reported values where available; limitation L-05. Each deficiency is also recorded in the Bank data issue register (DI-2027-0142 to DI-2027-0146) with a remediation owner and target date, for example DD-CTR-02: ESG Data Lead, registered label coverage of 75% of mortgage exposure by 31 December 2028 through the EP-Online interface for new valuations. A deficiency is closed only on confirmed remediation, after which the related conservative adjustment is reassessed. The deficiencies and their impact on the reliability of the aggregated results are explained in the ICAAP results pack.

sections.heading: Remediation at source and escalation
sections.text: Deficiencies are remediated at source where feasible: DD-CTR-01 by correcting address data in CVD (212 corrections completed in February 2027), DD-CTR-04 by the CRDH Data Steward correcting the NACE codes of 64 holding companies, and DD-CTR-05 by a vendor data refresh scheduled for September 2027. Correction only in the RDS is limited to the imputation and re-mapping steps documented in sections 4.3 and 4.1.4. Corrections not supported by documented source evidence (the re-mapping of the remaining 148 holding companies) are treated as expert judgement and approved under MRM-STD-023 (EJ-CTR-02). No deficiency is rated high or critical under the Bank data issue framework; DD-CTR-02 is rated medium and would be escalated to the Group Data Governance Committee and the Model Risk Committee if registered label coverage fell below the red threshold of 55% of exposure.

sections.heading: Personal data and fair treatment
sections.text: The mortgage part of the RDS contains personal data of borrowers (loan identifiers, income and property address), processed under Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR for the Bank's legal obligations under the CRR and CRD to assess its capital adequacy. The processing is covered by the DPIA for credit risk modelling DPIA-2026-118, extended to CTR on 14 December 2026 (DPIA-2026-118-A2). The RDS contains no protected attributes; addresses are used only to match energy labels and are pseudonymised after matching. CTR does not produce outputs on individual customers: the mortgage module is applied at loan level for aggregation only, and its results are not used in credit decisions, pricing or customer communication.

sections.heading: Reproducibility
sections.text: The RDS is built by versioned code in repository ctr-climate (Sustainability Risk Modelling group of the Bank's GitLab), build code tag rds-v1.0.0 (commit 4e91c2a). Source snapshots are those of 31 December 2026 for the portfolio, the frozen RDS-MORT-NL v4.0 for the affordability panel, the Kadaster delivery of 15 January 2026 and the corporate rating system extract of 12 January 2026. The software environment is recorded in the lock file of the tag (Python 3.11.9, pandas 2.2.2, pyarrow 16.1.0). A full rebuild from source by a second developer on 5 March 2027 reproduced the frozen RDS exactly: 612,400 mortgage loan records, 3,850 obligor records, 7,301,882 panel account-months with 2,380 default events, 1,200,700 hedonic transactions and 36,960 corporate obligor-years with 540 default events. The frozen RDS is stored read-only as RDS-CTR-2026Q4 v1.0 in the model data lake (zone mdl-frozen, write access revoked for all developer roles), and this identifier is referenced in the MDD. This documentation, Annex A and the tagged build code allow Model Validation to rebuild the RDS independently from the source snapshots.

sections.heading: Archiving and retention
sections.text: Each RDS version used for development or recalibration (currently RDS-CTR-2026Q4 v1.0) is archived together with the build code tag, the lineage version and a snapshot of the catalogue metadata, so that the development data can be reproduced. Archived versions are retained for the life of the model and for at least ten years after its decommissioning, in line with the MRM retention schedule. Archived data are write-protected; a correction is made only by creating a new RDS version (for example v1.1) while the original version is retained.

sections.heading: Expert judgement in data treatment
sections.text: Three expert judgements in data treatment are recorded in the CTR expert judgement log (CTR-EJ v1.2, stored with the model documentation and referenced in MDD chapter 11): EJ-CTR-01 (neighbourhood modal label imputation for failed address matches), EJ-CTR-02 (re-mapping of 212 holding companies to activity sectors) and EJ-CTR-03 (conversion of pre-2021 labels to NTA 8800 classes with the RVO conversion table). Each entry records the type, life-cycle stage and affected data, the rationale, evidence relied on and alternatives rejected, the quantified impact, the proposer, the approver and approval date, and the review date and expiry condition. For example, EJ-CTR-02 was proposed by the lead developer, challenged by the Credit Risk Management sector analyst for energy and industry (challenge and resolution recorded in the log), and approved by the Model Owner and the Head of Risk Modelling on 22 February 2027 as medium materiality (impact +1.8% on corporate losses). EJ-CTR-01 and EJ-CTR-03 are of low materiality (impact below 1% of mortgage losses); they were proposed by T. Mulder and approved by the Model Owner. All three judgements are reviewed at each annual model review and when new data could replace them; EJ-CTR-01 and EJ-CTR-02 expire when deficiencies DD-CTR-01 and DD-CTR-04 are remediated at source.

sections.heading: Annex A – Data dictionary and lineage
sections.text: Annex A lists all 64 RDS variables: 47 retained model inputs and target constituents, and 17 discarded variables used to construct retained variables. For each variable it states the business definition, the source system and field, the transformation, the lineage path with ETL job or build script reference, and the extraction frequency. Example: COLL_LABEL_REG – registered energy label class valid at the reference date; source EP-Online bulk file field 'Energieklasse' via ESGDP table esg_lz.ep_online_labels; transformation: latest label with registration date not later than the reference date per BAG verblijfsobject-ID, NTA 8800 classes A++++ to G; build script rds/mortgage/labels.py; monthly. sections.heading: Purpose, scope and intended use
sections.text: CTR quantifies the impact of climate transition risk on the credit risk of the Bank's Dutch residential mortgage portfolio and of its corporate lending portfolio in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. Its primary uses are (a) the climate component of the ICAAP normative adverse scenario over 2027–2029, (b) the internal capital add-on for climate transition risk in the ICAAP economic perspective, and (c) the annual internal climate stress test with long-term scenario analysis to 2050 under ERM-STD-300 §10 and EBA/GL/2025/04. Secondary uses are the quantitative input to the annual C&E materiality assessment (CER-POL-001 §5), the forward-looking metrics of the prudential transition plan and the calibration of sector concentration thresholds by Credit Risk Management. CTR is not used for own funds requirements, IFRS 9 expected credit loss, pricing or individual credit decisions. Users are Enterprise Stress Testing (execution of runs), Capital Management (ICAAP), Sustainability Risk (materiality assessment) and Credit Risk Management (sector policies). The purpose of each analysis is defined in advance: the short-term analysis tests capital adequacy, the long-term analysis tests the resilience of the business model, and neither is a forecast; the expectations and limitations of each analysis are stated with its results (section 8.3).

sections.heading: Regulatory context and applicable requirements
sections.text: CTR implements CER-POL-001 §7–§11 and ERM-STD-300 §10, and addresses EBA/GL/2025/01, EBA/GL/2025/04, the ECB Guide on climate-related and environmental risks (Expectations 7, 8 and 11) and the ECB Guide to the ICAAP (Principles 3, 6 and 7). The applicable requirement set was derived from the Bank's requirement library at the start of development (requirement set RS-MDL19-01 of 2 October 2026) and was used to plan the evidence and the structure of this MDD and of the RDS documentation. CTR is a quantitative method whose output is used for risk measurement and reporting; it is therefore a model under MRM-POL-001 and is managed across the full model lifecycle, developed under MRM-STD-020 and documented under MRM-STD-021. The model was assessed against the AI system definition of Art. 3(1) AI Act: CTR is estimated with classical econometric methods (ordinary least squares and logistic regression) and applied as fixed, documented equations with expert-calibrated parameters, and in line with the Commission Guidelines on the definition of an AI system it is assessed as not being an AI system; this conclusion was recorded in the model inventory on 21 September 2026, before gate G1.

sections.heading: Model inventory record and tiering
sections.text: A model identification questionnaire (MIQ-2026-044) was submitted to MRM on 1 September 2026, and MRM concluded on 18 September 2026, within 20 business days, that CTR is a model and recorded the rationale. CTR was registered in the model inventory under identifier MDL-19 on 21 September 2026 (gate G0), before development started; version 1.0 is the version described in this document. The inventory record states the model name, version, purpose, intended and secondary uses, scope of application (Dutch residential mortgages and corporate lending in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany), risk type (climate transition risk as a driver of credit risk), regulatory use (ICAAP and stress testing) and model family (statistical). The model owner is M. de Groot, Head of Sustainability Risk Modelling, a 1LoD senior manager who remains accountable for the tasks delegated to the lead developer; the developers are the Sustainability Risk Modelling team, the main users Enterprise Stress Testing and Capital Management, and the assigned validation team Model Validation – Enterprise Risk. The model owner proposed the tier with the tiering template, scoring materiality High on criterion (a), since the portfolios covered exceed EUR 10 billion, and complexity High (scenario-based methodology, dependencies on five other models, extensive expert judgement). sections.heading: Lifecycle status and governance
sections.text: CTR is in the development stage: gate G0 was passed on 21 September 2026 and gate G1 (development sign-off) is planned for 25 June 2027, after completion of the 1LoD self-assessment against RS-MDL19-01. No gate is passed before the preceding gates are complete, and each gate decision and its evidence are recorded in the model inventory. After G1 the model will be submitted to Model Validation – Enterprise Risk for a full-scope initial validation (G2, planned July–September 2027); approval for use (G3) lies with the Model Approval Panel, whose decision is reported to the MRC at its next meeting, and go-live (G4) is planned for November 2027, before the 2027 climate stress test and the ICAAP 2028 cycle. The model will be validated independently before first use and after every material change, and periodically at least every two years as a Tier 2 model, counted from the previous validation opinion. The validators assigned to CTR have not contributed to its development; an Enterprise Stress Testing modeller who moved to Model Validation in January 2026 and contributed to the scenario design has been excluded from the validation team. CTR will not be used with a Not fit for purpose opinion, and any conditions attached to a Fit for purpose with conditions opinion will be recorded in the MRC conditions register with an owner and a deadline. For every open high- or medium-severity finding, the model owner will submit a remediation plan within 20 business days of the final validation report. The approval request will contain the validation opinion, the 1LoD self-assessment, open findings, known limitations and the conservative adjustments of chapter 6. Until CTR is approved, the ICAAP continues to use the interim expert-based climate add-on of EUR 190 million, approved by the Enterprise Risk Committee on 14 March 2026.
